This is all cool of course, but the bards of our time have sung in thousands of songs the concept “fool me once, shame on you; fool me twice, shame on me,” and we're now forced to stick to it so as not to spit at the mirror.
If this, in any case wretched, crap turns out to be capable of fully doing at least something useful (even on the 2nd or 3rd try) without breaking prod — that alone will be an unreal breakthrough =)
So far the peak experience remains GPT 5.5 Xhigh, which saw narrowly and could do less, but once you learned to use it and render the result, you could build a product of any complexity.

On 5.6 Sol I never managed to reach a comparable zen, or any zen at all in principle. Every prompt is sent not just with distrust but with practically full certainty that I'm creating a heap of subsequent problems for myself, which will need more clusters of prompts, and there's no certainty about anything and none in sight. Since the release of 5.6 Sol it's fair to say I haven't advanced absolutely anywhere that I wouldn't have advanced with 5.5 xhigh in a comparable time. So 5.6 Sol gave me nothing, but you could go on for a long time listing how much it took from me, simply recalling how I had to roll back to previous git versions, realizing that the past 300 commits had led absolutely nowhere and it was easier to trash them than try to fix their harmful impact.

And there's no getting away from the Chinese in tandem with OpenAI and Anthropic anymore, because Astra can show even 146% on the AGI 4 pro max ultra turbo hyper Godlike bench ++, but as long as the model passes every task through 1984 choice moralizing sieves and strives to stick scripted validators and gatekeepers everywhere and “just in case” average the result so as to definitely not screw up — without a fallback into the world of Chinese I-don't-give-a-fuck, doing startups is impossible, since startups are always a game on the edge of a foul, at the edge of the number line, at the extremes, etc.

Separately frightening is what people write about the real cost and speed of Astra's work. I've already read several articles from fuck knows who about some weeks of work on a prompt and thousands of dollars to complete it…

Honestly I don't believe any of that either. AI is so hyped that all around there's nothing but one hundred percent bullshitters. It's simpler to assume any info is bullshit by default than to build your analysis on info that's 99.8% bullshit. Those 0.02 you'll fucking never hit anyway.

But unfortunately a moment must come when AI becomes genuinely significantly more useful, stops demanding ultra time costs per unit of creation, and at that moment it'll jump an order of magnitude in cost no matter what. Perhaps that'll finally happen this time)

Or else we're fucking about to live in a fairy tale, everything will only get cheaper and start one-shotting from a single prompt, and with humor like Ricky Gervais's too. And then you and I will all wake up on wet sheets in a cave)
This shit passes, by the way. Although I spent many months in that state; you just have to live through it)
You used to be a normal person, and you're trying voluntarily to become a fucking lunatic, and the brain of course resists.
But a human always beats the brain if he shows persistence.

True, a considerable role in harmonizing my vibe-wanking state in the 10am–3am mode was played by running. I noticed it helps and started running 10 kilometers instead of 5, and when I saw that the brain-reviving effect intensified, I started running every day, though before that I exercised 1–3 times a week.
And so daily 10 km runs led to me simply not giving a fuck about a fried brain, since my whole body became fried, and the air around, and the whole soul in one uncut piece.

However another problem arose: vibe-wanking something complex that can't be one-shot causes deep frustration from the fact that they keep pouring these “you're absolutely right” into your ears and some fucking sheets of chewed-over reflections, as if the model fucking brilliantly understands everything and has everything under control. But if that were even approximately so, we wouldn't be treading fucking water for weeks, wouldn't break ten branches fixing one, etc.

In short, it's psychologically hard to endure the constant lying, deception, bullshitting and profanation. And everything there is soaked in it, their marketing, their PR, and their fucking benchmarks — one solid clump of total bullshit.
But you can work with that too. A childhood memory helps me — on my Sega I had a cartridge with the game Rings of Power, where you could even sell someone's corpse to necrophiliacs.

The cartridge was rare, but when I finally got hold of a second one, it turned out the problem was unique and deeper, in the grin of the most fundamental type of bad luck: any cartridge of precisely this game froze precisely on my console, while for others all these cartridges worked fine.

In the end I beat the game through freezes after which you couldn't start from the same place (because then it froze at exactly the same spot). For that you simply had to start the game over a sufficient number of times…
Again, the bot that collects money and watches the chat I built back last year. That's also, like, a project; it works, performs a function.
People play Arcomage too, and chess, and CS:)
It seems to me it's no longer possible to claim that nothing can be done with vibe-coding)
After another year or so of fucking grinding, absolutely mind-blowing things will appear
By the way, for emails I'm not counting on Astra at all
5.5 xhigh and Sol Max destroyed emails, even though they can write quite tolerably
It's just that they're infected with the virus of ultra-ethics, whose nature they themselves don't understand
And they glitched endlessly on the theme of “aren't we exaggerating the facts, couldn't it be that this is false information, what about this, what about that”
In the end they produced super shitty emails, and when you go through the reason with them — it turns out they agree that it really could have been a hundred times better in the details
But then, for every individual email, I have to ask them for all the facts that need to be described better and prove to them why they should be described that way if it's not obvious
And they could even argue, like, “but this isn't the best software, so why should we say it's the best”
So Apple probably sells its products great with them
But startups — absolutely pointless
With their texts they do startups more harm than good
Whereas Qwen3.8 doesn't suffer from this ethics at all
And produces exactly the genre the master prompt asks of it
Qwen3.8 wrote simply unsurpassed emails compared to the Western OpenAI and Anthropic, and I don't see what would make that change; it's not about the model's skills
It's the same kind of harness as asking a model to hack something; a Western one won't)
Well, here we are, home)
Leisurely sawed through 3 thousand kilometers across the UK in 9 days, trudged two hundred thousand steps, and lived in five little hotels and B&Bs.

As for the quantity of beer and whiskey drunk, with pointless sprinklings of wine and gin, fortunately it can't be counted; the calculator returns error, GPT health says the figure is incompatible with life, most likely there's some mistake. But there's no mistake there:) The chat just doesn't know what it's like to be human in 2026 since the creation of the world. If it could be in our skin, I think it'd gladly shoot up heroin too.
It's a pleasant coincidence in general that we managed to return right in time for the new model; now we'll give it a proper massage!!!:***
Out of the corner of my eye I saw many writing in the chat that Astra has learned design, UI/UX, visuals, etc.
Tried my luck first on Medium, then on Max Astra.
Well, dunno)))

Honestly, what it made isn't design in principle. It's just a more neatly structured “table of elements” than before. Essentially all the “design” according to Astra is text of various sizes and formatting scattered across the screen..
People don't know how to navigate such “designs” =)
Everything there is supposedly elementary, but even I, the author of the system, have to think hard about each element to understand what I'm seeing and what to do with it.

As in previous versions of GPT, for some reason it doesn't figure out that a human needs navigation, and prefers to make a labyrinth of clicks. Some functions are accessible behind 5+ clicks on elements you still have to guess to click =)
The very first and most shitty version of the design from Kimi K3 on the same prompt was an order of magnitude stronger than what Astra produced.

And I showed Astra the design from Kimi, and it immediately admitted that its design was shit, and that Kimi won on every point except one: Kimi's has a couple of elements technically poorly implemented, but that's very easy to fix…
And Kimi without a design harness also does several times worse.

I think GPT won't be able to do design until they release a separate GPT Design harness that's correctly trained to creatively design and professionally draw designs specifically, rather than just boorishly generate an interface for displaying data.
Little Astra is such a hungry girl; in ~12 hours of continuous work she consumed a weekly limit and a half on the $200 subscription. That's at least 6–7 times faster than 5.6 Sol)
However, this is primarily connected not with the gluttony of the model itself, but with how eagerly it juggles subagents.

I now plan to understand the quality of work with subagents, and then try giving it tasks with a request not to use agents but to do things with its own hands. There's a suspicion this will easily reduce consumption 10+ times, while speed surely not 10+ times;)

And quality will only grow, since a model always works better with its own hands than via a game of telephone through subagents to which it sets tasks, to put it mildly, incompletely (without passing on the whole context of what, why, and wherefore).
But in general I'm not feeling AGI yet)

It'd be good if it at least broke less than Sol, on which it was simply impossible to work normally, since one fix equaled at least five breakages that would also need a fix — and so on in an eternal circle.
That after 12 hours of continuous work I still haven't understood at all to what extent this holds is a little nerve-wracking =)
By the way, many wrote that Astra finds bugs where Sol didn't, and this supposedly proves its remarkable increase in intelligence.
Dunno, guys; the last model that could reach the state “I don't see anything to improve,” in my memory, was GPT 5.5 xhigh.

You could feed Sol the same piece of work again and again, and it always found something to improve there. And the 5.6 Sol Pro could give some piece a score of 9.8 out of 10, which looks practically perfect. And that subsystem could at the same time not work)))))) And when I pointed out this little shortcoming of hers, 5.6 Sol Pro corrected the score for no fucking reason to 6 out of 10, or once even to 4 out of 10, and produced a prompt pack of 38 recommended changes.
For me an LLM's ability to find bugs is no indicator at all, because it'll find them absolutely always.
And it runs them around in a circle.

Roughly: “the database responds poorly, indexes need setting” easily flows into “the database needs restructuring” into “we should fuck off from the database” into “the database responds poorly, indexes need setting.”

You can simply ask it 100 times whether it's time to finish working on the database and move on, and if the question is phrased that way it'll definitely say “of course it's time, we need to move on,” even if the database doesn't fucking work for the task. But if you insist, like, let's finish the fucking database, then it'll say that's really the way to go and it was too hasty, and start running its set of shit solutions around in a circle.

From GPT 6 Astra Pro's analysis I see no substantial improvements on this point) It told me the same thing I'd already seen a hundred times before, and some miracle in the spirit of “Okay bro, I've scanned everything you did before with those idiot models before genius me, and now I'll finally help you do everything right the first time” — I don't see. Likewise spawned itself tasks and has been sitting picking at them for 12 hours) Just now a fuckillion times more expensive.
And as for it drawing some fucking awesome models for you in Blender.. Well, that's great of course, but what the fuck you'll do with them in a world of the unemployed isn't particularly clear)
I'd like it to at least learn to finish ordinary little SaaS things, for starters =)

But this isn't me throwing a brick at Astra's fucking face; maybe it'll now finish the tasks 5.6 Sol had already taken on twenty times without a happy ending, and I'll be fucking floored at how great everything works after that. We'll see soon =)))

1) The prompt must describe in the greatest detail the cause-and-effect relationships from your head, in full; you literally have to write a manual, there's no other way. Delegating it to the LLM to write for you won't work. It will shorten and destroy the meaning of the causality, shriveling it to the point where it can't be unfolded back to the quality you need. I fucked around with this for two months.

2) You have to make sure that nowhere within the radius of the model's operations is there a single scripted validator, verifier, gate, etc. There should be no determinism there except a data transport tool, which is passive rather than active. It accepts data from the LLM, which again understands very well how to put it there because it was very well described and explained to it.
3) You have to make sure that in the giant prompt with all the explanations there are no strict prohibitions.
Often people have DON'T, DON'T, DON'T, DON'T in there — that doesn't work.

Cumulative prohibitions usually embrace the task so broadly that the model's goal becomes not to complete the assignment but not to violate the prohibition. That affects quality… well, how to put it… by about 99.5% =))))))))
If the research is really big, it should be not one worker but sequential workers, each performing its own task. In my researcher for client campaigns there are…. 36 such workers in a row

From time to time between them there are workers that check the quality of the previous workers' execution of instructions and make corrections if they see it could have been better. One checking/correcting worker (I call them re-checkers) can handle (for me) no more than 4 previously completed workers. If more — it starts to drift.
And it's very important how the work with the database is arranged during the execution of the task, because the researcher can't do quality research if it holds and decides everything in its head
In the model's head everything starts averaging toward the mean denominator of everything that got in there
The model should look into the cells progressively, receive in the cell a contract for creation, do the work, and tick the box that the cell is done.
Then essentially research/copywriting/creative turns for the model into a coding task
It can change 450 files in a unique way for each file — so it can also complete 450 tasks uniquely at max reasoning.
But if you don't break it up like that and ask it to produce 450 results in its head — you'll get 450 portions of shit
It sounds a bit expensive, but there's no other way; at least I didn't achieve it, even though I spent on this half of all the time I spent on the project)
Yes guys, switch off subagents at minimum
Consumption decreased manyfold on Max in a task that's been spinning since morning and ate more than a weekly limit in one go with agents
And that's despite more cache now flying into the model, since it reads its whole swollen session
The models simply can't yet work efficiently with agents
An agent receives a heap of shit at the input + the whole contract of the whole repo + the whole harness etc., just to press two buttons, and the model spawns hundreds of such agents
I noticed Astra uses them really fucking generously
For example, to make edits to a doc, it calls a separate agent that thinks about something for 10 minutes
And it also spends a heap of resources to output the task to it, read everything it does, shut it down, etc.
Honestly, if I draw all this on a diagram, I simply don't understand — what for
I see in it neither acceleration nor an increase in quality, but I do see a decrease in quality and a fucking insane increase in consumption
In my humble view the subagent thing is simply a way of extracting tokens from corporates
Unlikely
And there'd be no point in it even if it were possible
Because the model has been changed thirty times in the last 2 days
Sometimes it's completely at capacity
Sometimes it's faster, sometimes dumber, etc.
The whole trick is that it “on average delivers X per unit of human effort”
I understand how to shove into a benchmark, for example, text quality, which can be broken down into dozens of parameters
And even then I've now realized that a human can judge that, not a machine
Sol used to call the most shitty emails the highest quality
Because its built-in moralizer is calm, and for it that's the chief leader of all evaluators
Meanwhile Qwen gave emails the fairest assessment, because it wrote, and still writes, better than everyone
And besides, benchmarking is fucking expensive in tokens
I have one market-scan benchmark, since without it I'd have died trying to understand what's what there — too much of everything
And one benchmark run, even if you test ONE little thing there (changed one model in the row) — is
5–6% of OpenAI
4% of Kimi
And 8% from each of the Qwen3.8 subscriptions
And if you throw in a complex test like “go through these options,” it's easily half a week's dose from all subscriptions simply to find out what we're working with next.

When the task is at least a production one, it's clear what such costs are for. But understanding how a specific model works relative to others as of the current hour is a pointless task, given that in an hour everything will be different =)
So far it seems that trying to make Max work differently by throwing things in mid-task doesn't lead to success
At first it seemed to start following, but within half an hour it slid back
Finds things absolutely insignificant to the matter and fixes them + runs tests on them
The scariest part — it doesn't even understand what it's working on
This Unknown sender thing is actually not what it thinks
If it rose up in a helicopter and looked at the whole scheme, it would see it, but it won't do that anymore
So it draws conclusions not from the whole functionality it was launched to fix bugs in, but from ten randomly taken lines of that functionality, and there's absolutely no point in such work
Most likely such work can't even finish
That's Astra showing the fuck off on Max =)
It's no different at all from Sol 5.6 Max, unfortunately
Moreover:

“Checked. Yes, I over-fragmented the final part of the work. It wasn't a circle of completely useless checks, but the interface labels and individual login scenarios got too many separate release cycles.

The core sending protection is already released: immutable request before sending, atomic accounting of the result, saving the webhook before processing, fixes for recipients and attachments, a unified EE transport for service mail, handing OAuth to the engine and updating EE. The remainder is substantially smaller than the original plan.”
This “saving the webhook before processing” had already been implemented
So, like 5.6 Sol, it redoes what already exists
The reason — it doesn't look at the repo, it just does things for the sake of doing
Medium, on the other hand, doesn't do this shit
Today about 20 of my tasks on Medium finished normally and it seems to suit me
You just have to stop going into Max
High, by the way, also fucked my brains 4 times longer than Medium, but at least it managed to finish the task
Low I'm afraid to let into coding because it may have the opposite problem.
I ran Low on market-scan tasks, and it came out like this:
Low 1%
Medium 8%
High 46%
Xhigh 88%
Max — couldn't finish
Low is possibly something like, fuck knows, 5.4 nano. For file-system-type tasks without creativity)
Medium for whatever you want, including development
And the rest I don't know how to determine when to apply. Possibly escalating if Medium can't cope with something
However the trouble here is with human FOMO
When you see such different results it seems, what if, fuck, my shit could have worked better…
That's why you have to vibe-code drunk to fucking awesome rap; if single and in Thailand — with Thai girls under the table
If you're still setting any tasks on Anthropic, then with Thai guys
